newsitem.title: GERMANY: INSTANT VIEW - BUNDESBANK REPO ANNOUNCEMENT.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - BUNDESBANK REPO ANNOUNCEMENT.

text.p: Following are economists' reactions after the Bundesbank kept its securities repurchase rate unchanged by setting this week's tender for securities repurchase agreements at an unchanged fixed rate of 3.00 percent.

UWE ANGENENDT, ECONOMIST BHF-BANK: "The Bundesbank's cautious stance remains intact because it has only set a repo tender for this week. So, speculation regarding a repo move has only been postponed until next week's tender announcement. But I don't think they'll change the tender next week so soon before the Bundesbank's next council meeting on August 21. I expect the dollar to rise on this announcement. The Bundesbank is clearly reserving the option to decide on its repo policy from week to week. I think we are seeing a turnaround on the price trend although (that) does not mean a major rise in inflation. We see the repo rate rising to 3.50 percent by the end of the year.

JOERG KRAEMER, MERRILL LYNCH -- "It was expected. Last week, Welteke (Bundesbank council member Ernst) told us he was against rate hikes. The Bundesbank will not start the rate hike process without broad-based support on the council. The dollar needs to climb over 1.90 marks to win over doves on the council. I see a 75-percent chance that the Bundesbank will start the rate hike process within the next three months. The most likely case is they will switch to a variable repo because then, they could blame the market for higher rates."
PETRA KOEHLER, ECONOMIST AT DRESDNER BANK IN FRANKFURT:

"Because of the dollar, which is not as strong as it was last week, the Bundesbank has won a bit more time. But nevertheless I think that after the holidays there is a very good chance the Bundesbank will raise interest rates.
"Even at the next repo or in the coming weeks we expect the repo to rise to around 3.20 percent as a first step."
